prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance (bag-drop/transfer induction) through screening, sorting, make-up, to outbound load control handoff. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (stages bag, flight unchanged; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk); Bag Tag Printer (unique-ID tag; Calibration Witness Tag, used by Maintenance Technician to verify calibration witnessed before return to service; replacement tag only after authorized confirmation); Transfer Bag Feeder (no check bypass; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station); Induction Tray Conveyor (metering; priority admission after scan); Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (tag-flight association; routing, screening profile, sort plan; exceptions to Secondary Inspection Chute; cutoff profiles; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; records disposition/release; checks identity vs routing before disposition; authorizes rejoin of assigned path after identity/flight checks pass); Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (induction permissive; Recovery Route Card; lane assignment; applies routing state without bypassing screening); Flight Data Gateway, alias Lantern (flight identity/timing, destination/service date; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory); Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (Chute Occupancy Note; routes by destination/status/cutoff; holds bag during unresolved manual disposition); North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel (tag read/image for identity check), South Gate Scanner (Manual Rescan Receipt, used by Desk to confirm approved second image); Image Resolution Desk (presents image/exception to operator; operator compares features vs tag/handling data, requires legible image, requests physical inspection if inconclusive); Secondary Inspection Chute (controlled physical exam location; retains until disposition); Bag Reconciliation Station (Bag Match Query; records flight match); East/West Make-Up Conveyor; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit, alias Orchard (receives Carousel Release Slip); Outbound Load Control Desk (confirms load eligibility; reconciles before closeout). Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (recovery, priorities; approves dispositions beyond operator authority; make-up release within window); Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (security exams; Custody Seal Log); Security Duty Manager (security holds); Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator (sends Carousel Release Slip; confirms flight-side constraints). States: clear, exception, awaiting review, hold. Requirements: hold missing/conflicting/oversized; mismatch holds until resolved/escalated; tag must be attached and match record; changed route/flight

New part:
S178: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S179: Safe operation depends on keeping people clear of moving equipment and maintaining a controlled path for every bag.
S180: The Baggage Operations Supervisor may stop induction when an unsafe condition, uncertain bag location, or loss of control is reported.
S181: A stop command places the affected equipment in a defined safe state without disabling unrelated routes that remain safe to operate.
S182: Before entering a conveyor or sorter hazard zone, the Maintenance Technician isolates the relevant energy sources and verifies that movement has stopped.
S183: Guards and access panels remain in place during operation, and bypasses are permitted only under an approved maintenance procedure.
S184: The Baggage Operations Supervisor uses the occupancy note to confirm that a chute can safely accept bags.
S185: The Maintenance Technician consults the Recovery Route Card before returning equipment to service after a route change.
S186: Pebble secures the response area and directs handling of any bag referred for explosives assessment.
S187: The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.
S188: A scanner fault requires the affected feed to be held until the fault is assessed and the bag disposition is known.
S189: The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
S190: Lantern supplies current flight data so that operating routes can be checked against active assignments.
S191: The Baggage Control System records equipment alarms and presents the affected route for review by authorized personnel.
S192: When the Induction Tray Conveyor stops unexpectedly, staff prevent further bag entry and keep the approach area clear.
S193: The Maintenance Technician removes a jam only after confirming isolation and arranging safe access to the blockage.
S194: The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification when a bag's location or identity is uncertain after an interruption.
S195: East Make-Up Conveyor runs only after its guards are confirmed closed and its downstream capacity is available.
S196: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is held from receiving bags when its discharge area is obstructed or its operating status is uncertain.
S197: The Maintenance Technician performs corrective work and reports any condition that prevents safe restart.
S198: The Baggage Operations Supervisor controls the operational hold, communicates its scope, and confirms that affected staff understand the restriction.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response: {"summary":"Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to outbound load handoff. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor, alias Tern (approvals, release; may stop induction on unsafe/uncertain/loss of control; controls operational hold, communicates scope); Explosives Response Team, alias Pebble (Custody Seal Log; secures response area); Security Duty Manager (holds; access control); Maintenance Technician (isolates energy, verifies stop before hazard zones; consults Recovery Route Card after route change; inspects before clearing faults; reports restart-blocking conditions); Airline Ramp Coordinator (sends Carousel Release Slip).
